info:
These are the names of the letters (symbols) of the Korean alphabet, Hangul, an alphabet with a unique system.
Hangul letters are not written linearly like English, but are grouped into syllable blocks.
1. Letters = Basic Building Blocks (Jamo / 자모)
There are two main types of letters in Hangul:
•        Consonants (자음): e.g., ㄱ, ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ, ㅇ
•        Vowels (모음): e.g., ㅏ, ㅓ, ㅗ, ㅣ
These are called jamo — the smallest units, like letters in English.
But:
➡ Korean does not write these letters by themselves in actual writing.
➡ Instead, they are combined into syllables.
2. Syllables = Letter Blocks
Every written Korean syllable is made up of a syllable block (음절).
Each block combines 2–3 letters in this order:
[Initial consonant] + [Vowel] (+ [Final consonant])
For example:
Block        Letters inside        Pronounced
가        ㄱ + ㅏ        "ga"
밥        ㅂ + ㅏ + ㅂ        "bap"
3. What if a syllable starts with a vowel?
Korean syllables can’t begin with a vowel by itself — it needs an initial consonant.
So Korean uses the placeholder consonant:
ㅇ (이응 / i-eung)
•        When ㅇ is at the beginning of a syllable, it is silent.
•        Its only purpose is to fill the initial consonant slot.
Examples:
Vowel        Syllable block        Pronounced
ㅏ        아 (ㅇ + ㅏ)        "a"
ㅗ        오 (ㅇ + ㅗ)        "o"
answer: ㄱ - 기역 (gi-yeok) - g/k: "g" at the start of a syllable, "k" at the end.
goal_words: - 기역 (gi-yeok) - g/k: "g" at the start of a syllable,  "k" at the end.
